scores.evidence: Phase 2 "Depends on: Phase 1, the eval set"; Phase 3 "Depends on: V3"; Phase 4 "Depends on: V1, V3, Phase 3"
scores.rationale: Phases run substrate → defenses → retrieval → model hardening → canary, each with explicit dependencies and validation gates before the next.

scores.evidence: an internal staff member asks "How do I reset my password?" and gets a streamed answer citing the right article.
scores.rationale: Phase 0 is a real end-to-end slice deployed via CI/CD behind a flag with tracing, alerts and rollback, verified by V0.

scores.evidence: Build vs buy ... Flip condition: The vendor passes V3 at lower total cost → buy
scores.rationale: Irreversible decisions have reversibility class, default, assumption, validation and flip condition, and unknowns are labeled.

scores.evidence: Phase 1 tasks: masking, output filter, injection suite, caps, then handoff
scores.rationale: Broad defenses and schema-wide concerns mostly come before leaf work, but blast-radius ordering within phases isn't explicit and some ordering is loose (e.g., load test last).

scores.evidence: Phase 0: "Allow-list access, secrets in a vault, user and retrieved text treated as data"
scores.rationale: Security has concrete content in every phase 0–4 in the cross-cutting table and in the phase tasks.

scores.evidence: OpenTelemetry traces cover every step, with token counts, cost and latency. Alerts fire on errors and cost.
scores.rationale: Observability is concrete in Phase 0 and every later phase (retrieval scores, eval tracking, canary dashboards).

scores.evidence: Infrastructure as code, pinned model and embedding model
scores.rationale: Reproducibility is addressed per phase: IaC, pinned models, versioned evals/index/prompts, CI injection suite, rollout config snapshot.

scores.evidence: Timeout plus degraded reply, handoff; Index alias rollback; Fallback model, load test
scores.rationale: Failure handling appears concretely in every phase starting with Phase 0 flag-off rollback and injected LLM failure.

scores.evidence: Phase 0 wraps text as data, no tools, hard caps; Phase 1 defenses, budgets, handoff; then retrieval (2), model access/memory (3), feedback (4)
scores.rationale: Defenses, budgets and human-in-the-loop precede retrieval, then model access, memory, orchestration, routing (deferred) and feedback in the right order.

scores.evidence: Routing between models: when V4 fails on cost. Long-term memory: when users repeatedly have to re-explain context
scores.rationale: Deferred items are listed each with a pull-forward condition.

note: Very strong, well-ordered plan; only weakness is that within-phase blast-radius ordering is implicit rather than reasoned.
